description_full: Agilysys, Inc. operates as a developer and marketer of software-enabled solutions and services to the hospitality industry in North America, Europe, the Asia-Pacific, and India. The company offers software solutions fully integrated with third party hardware and operating systems; cloud applications, support, and maintenance; subscription and maintenance; and professional services. Its hospitality software solutions comprise hospitality experience cloud offers solution ecosystems that combine core operational systems for property management, point-of-sale (POS), and inventory and procurement; and Hospitality Solution Studios. The company also provides food and beverage ecosystem solutions, such as the InfoGenesis POS, IG Kiosk, a self-service, customer-facing kiosk point of sale solution; and IG KDS, a digital kitchen management solution. Its food and beverage experience enhancer solutions include IG OnDemand; IG Fly; IG Quick Pay payment solution; IG Smart Menu; IG Digital Menu Board; IG PanOptic; Pay; eCash; gift card solution; and Analyze. In addition, the company offers hospitality and leisure ecosystem solutions comprising LMS, an on-premises or hosted, web, and mobile-enabled PMS solution; Versa; and Stay, a cloud-native SaaS property management system. Its hospitality and leisure and experience enhancer solutions consist of Book, Express Kiosk and Express Mobile for check-in and check-out; Spa software; Golf; Sales and Catering; Service; Authorize; DataMagine; Reserve solution; Digital Marketing solution; Retail POS solution; Central Reservations; Loyalty and Promotions; Membership; Residence Management; and Guest App. Further, the company provides inventory and procurement ecosystem solutions, including the Eatec solution and Stratton Warren System. The company was formerly known as Pioneer-Standard Electronics, Inc. and changed its name to Agilysys, Inc. in 2003. Agilysys, Inc. was founded in 1932 and is headquartered in Alpharetta, Georgia.

financial_summary: Agilysys, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.4B market cap on $319M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +17% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 16% against a 9% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it. Gross margins of 61% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $68M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.80× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 87× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 3.6% of the shares.

prof: ROIC of 16% clears the cost of capital of 8.6% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 4.32).
It runs a 61% gross margin and converts 21% of revenue into free cash flow, or 15% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.80x.
ROE of 12% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.5x equity multiplier).

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $116.9M (3% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 15.0, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 17.3% over 3 years, 18.4% over 5 years and 9.6% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 20%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 16.2% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 20.3% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a backlog worth 48% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 44%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (0.6% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.6%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (13 sales, net $23.9M sold).
The share count has grown 2.7% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 2,413 employees, each generates about $132K of revenue, 0.4x the Technology median, and revenue has grown 2.9% a year across its filed history.
